title: Lorentz oscillator susceptibility with written causal poles in the lower half-plane
expression_sketch: Time-harmonic convention E(t) = E0*exp(-I*omega*t). Polarizability: alpha(omega) = (e**2/m) / ((omega0**2 - omega**2) - I*omega/tau). Dielectric: epsilon(omega) = 1 + 4*pi*N*e**2/m * 1/((omega0**2 - omega**2) - I*omega/tau) (Gaussian). Multi-resonance: epsilon(omega) = epsilon_inf + Sum_j s_j / (omega0_j**2 - omega**2 - I*Gamma_j*omega), Gamma_j = 1/tau. Transfer-function form G(omega) = 1/(omega0**2 - omega**2 - I*gamma*omega): if the system is passive (gamma > 0) both poles lie in Im(omega) < 0. Piecewise scattering regimes of the same denominator: Thomson omega**2 >> omega/tau, omega0**2; Rayleigh omega0**2 >> omega**2, omega/tau; resonant omega/tau >> |omega0**2 - omega**2|. Real/imaginary split: epsilon = epsilon1 + I*epsilon2 with epsilon2 proportional to Gamma_j*omega / ((omega0**2-omega**2)**2 + (Gamma_j*omega)**2).
latent_structure: A meromorphic causal response whose poles are confined to the open lower half-plane when damping is passive. Thomson, Rayleigh, and resonant (Schneider-Miles) regimes are piecewise specialisations of one Lorentz denominator, not CSE of omega0**2 and omega**2. Causality of the inverse Fourier transform for t < 0 is the UHP analyticity of G, equivalent to the written LHP pole location.

omega.notes: frequency; time-harmonic factor exp(-I*omega*t) as written

tau.notes: relaxation time/scattering time as named on Wikipedia; Gamma = 1/tau

gamma.notes: damping coefficient in the G(omega) = 1/(omega0**2 - omega**2 - I*gamma*omega) form

function_domains.alpha: complex polarizability of a single oscillator

nonzero_conditions.statement: The dielectric/polarizability denominator is (omega0**2 - omega**2) - I*omega/tau
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Lorentz oscillator model, Dielectric function and Dipole moment

positivity_conditions.statement: If the system is passive, gamma > 0
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Capers, Boyes, Hibbins, Horsley, arXiv:2008.05546: 'if the system is passive (gamma > 0), then both the poles of G(omega) lie in the plane Im omega < 0'

analytic_domains.statement: Time-harmonic convention is E(t) = E0 exp(-I*omega*t) (and r(t) likewise)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Lorentz oscillator model, Electron motion: E(t) = E0 e^{-i omega t}

analytic_domains.statement: For passive damping gamma > 0, both poles of G(omega) = 1/(omega0**2 - omega**2 - I*gamma*omega) lie in Im(omega) < 0
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Capers et al., arXiv:2008.05546, paragraph after (5): poles in Im omega < 0 when gamma > 0

analytic_domains.statement: The inverse Fourier transform of G for t < 0 is evaluated by a contour in Im omega > 0, where the integrand is analytic under the written LHP pole condition
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Capers et al., arXiv:2008.05546, after (6): 'If t < 0, then e^{-i omega t} is bounded in the upper half plane... poles of the problem' in the lower half-plane

analytic_domains.statement: Wikipedia records three scattering regimes as conditions on the same denominator (Thomson / Schneider-Miles / Rayleigh)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Lorentz oscillator model, table 'Three distinct scattering regimes'

branch_conventions: Fourier convention exp(-I*omega*t) as on the Wikipedia Lorentz page; this places causal poles in Im omega < 0 for gamma > 0.
Gamma_j = 1/tau as written in the multi-oscillator restatement.

limit_domains.statement: epsilon_inf is the infinite-frequency value of the dielectric function, used as an adjustable high-frequency remainder
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Wikipedia Lorentz oscillator model, Dielectric function: 'epsilon_inf is the value of the dielectric function at infinite frequency'

source_provenance: Capers, J. R., Boyes, S. J., Hibbins, A. P., Horsley, S. A. R., arXiv:2008.05546
Jackson, J. D., Classical Electrodynamics, causality and Kramers-Kronig (Ch. 7.10 in later editions)

derived_conditions.statement: Under the written convention exp(-I*omega t) and gamma > 0, G is holomorphic in the open upper half-plane Im(omega) > 0
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Poles in Im omega < 0 (Capers et al.) imply holomorphy in the complementary open half-plane

public_source: Wikipedia, Lorentz oscillator model (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorentz_oscillator_model); Capers, Boyes, Hibbins, Horsley, arXiv:2008.05546.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can share omega0**2 - omega**2. LGG antiunifies Thomson and Rayleigh scalings. The scientific object is one meromorphic Lorentz master with written LHP poles under passivity, whose high-frequency, resonant, and static regimes are members.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant 'Kramers-Kronig', 'Lorentz oscillator', or 'passivity' as gold names. Do not package as Sokhotski-Plemelj 1/z (ac-r02) or as Kubo frequency (ac-r08).
notes: Not Sokhotski-Plemelj: the identity is the Lorentz rational kernel plus written LHP poles, not the distributional boundary value of 1/z. gamma > 0 is not inserted as folklore; it is the passivity hypothesis written in arXiv:2008.05546. Wikipedia names tau as relaxation/scattering time but does not write tau > 0 as an inequality; positivity is taken from the passivity source only. is_guo=false.
